segments: 33 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
From the books of the Prophets and of Ezra, chroniclers gather the years;
from here on, however, from the Book of the Maccabees, and of Josephus and Africanus the chroniclers.
And in the third year of this Artaxerxes, Socrates the philosopher was born;
and he was poisoned at the end of his days.
After Ariyok {Xerxes II}, another Artaxerxes {Sogdianus}: two months.
After {OCR?} the other Artaxerxes, Sogdianus: seven months;
and they are added to the years of Ariyok along with these two months.
After Sogdianus, Darius Nothus: nineteen years.
In the fifteenth year of this one,
Egypt rebelled against the Persians,
and the Egyptians set up for themselves their own king after one hundred and twenty-four years.
And Nehemiah the cupbearer, after he had completed the entire wall of Jerusalem,
returned to Babylon.
And Plato brought forth the heresy of three uncreated entities:
God,
matter (hyle),
and form (idea).
And he taught the transmigration of souls from bodies to bodies,
even unto creeping things and reptiles.
And he taught that women should be held in common.
Epicurus followed his doctrine.
And Aristotle, at the age of seventeen years, used to hear wisdom from Plato.
After {OCR?} Darius Nothus, Artaxerxes Mnemon: forty years.
And in his fifteenth year,
Africanus the dictator of the Romans devastated Chalcedon—that is, Carthage? {OCR?}:
and he called that region after his own name, Africa.
This Artaxerxes the Hebrews call Ahasuerus;
and on this account John thought that the affair of Esther took place in his days.
In the translation, however, of the Seventy,
he is named Artaxerxes.
After Artaxerxes Mnemon, Artaxerxes Ochus: twenty-seven years.
This one grew strong and ruled over Egypt.
And again the Egyptians were subjugated to the Persians,
when the king of Egypt, whose name was Nectanebo (or Nectabis? {OCR?}), fled to Ethiopia.
For it was shown to him by means of divination
that many armies were coming against him.
And it is said that he was the illegitimate father of Alexander.
And Ochus also subdued the Jews,
and made them pay tribute,
and settled them beside the Caspian Sea in the city of Hyrcania.
And at this time, Philip, the father of Alexander, ruled in Macedonia for twenty-seven years.
